title: Finding Piecewise Formulas for Discontinuous Two-Segment Graphs
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find a piecewise formula for each graphed function: (a) a segment from (0, 2) (closed) to (2, 0) (closed), followed by a segment from (2, 1) (open) to (5, 0) (closed); (b) a segment from (-1, 0) (closed) to (0, -3) (open), followed by a segment from (0, 3) (closed) through (1, 1) to (2, -1) (closed).
finalAnswer: \text{(a) } f(x) = \begin{cases} 2 - x, & 0 \le x \le 2 \\ -\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{5}{3}, & 2 < x \le 5 \end{cases}; \quad \text{(b) } f(x) = \begin{cases} -3x - 3, & -1 \le x < 0 \\ -2x + 3, & 0 \le x \le 2 \end{cases}

steps.title: Derive the Two Branches of Graph (a)
steps.explanation: For graph (a), on 0 <= x <= 2 the segment from (0, 2) to (2, 0) has slope -1 and y-intercept 2, giving y = 2 - x. On 2 < x <= 5, the segment from the open circle (2, 1) to the closed dot (5, 0) has slope -1/3 and equation y = -x/3 + 5/3.
steps.why: The open circle at (2, 1) and closed dot at (2, 0) assign x = 2 to the first interval 0 <= x <= 2.

steps.title: Derive the Two Branches of Graph (b)
steps.explanation: For graph (b), on -1 <= x < 0 the segment from (-1, 0) to the open circle (0, -3) has slope -3 and y-intercept -3, giving y = -3x - 3. On 0 <= x <= 2, the segment from (0, 3) through (1, 1) to (2, -1) has slope -2 and y-intercept 3, giving y = -2x + 3.
steps.why: The closed dot at (0, 3) and open circle at (0, -3) place x = 0 in the second branch 0 <= x <= 2.

steps.title: State Both Piecewise Formulas
steps.mathExpression: \text{(a) } f(x) = \begin{cases} 2 - x, & 0 \le x \le 2 \\ -\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{5}{3}, & 2 < x \le 5 \end{cases}, \qquad \text{(b) } f(x) = \begin{cases} -3x - 3, & -1 \le x < 0 \\ -2x + 3, & 0 \le x \le 2 \end{cases}
steps.explanation: Combine the linear equations with their exact endpoint inclusion inequalities.
steps.why: Every point in the domain of each graph is accounted for by exactly one branch.
